title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 222 (Imposition of restrictions upon securities)

content.overview: Section 222 empowers the Tribunal, where it appears that there is good reason to find out the relevant facts about any securities of a company and that it is necessary to impose restrictions, to order that the securities shall be subject to such restrictions as to transfer, exercise of voting or other rights, payment of dividends, or issue of further securities, as may be specified, for a period not exceeding three years. The restrictions preserve the position while ownership or related misconduct is investigated.
content.glance: Tribunal may impose restrictions on transfer, voting rights, dividends or further issue of securities for up to three years where necessary to ascertain relevant facts in connection with investigation; preserves position during probe.
content.study: Where it appears to the Tribunal, in connection with any investigation under section 216 or on a complaint made by any person in this behalf, that there is good reason to find out the relevant facts about any securities issued or to be issued by a company and the Tribunal is of opinion that such facts cannot be found out unless certain restrictions are imposed, the Tribunal may by order direct that the securities shall be subject to such restrictions as may be specified for a period not exceeding three years. Current-law framing: connect to investigation under s. 216 or a complaint; establish good reason to find relevant facts about securities; Tribunal opinion that restrictions are necessary; order restricting transfer, voting, dividends or further issue for a period not exceeding three years.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: In connection with investigation under s. 216 or on a complaint; good reason to find relevant facts about securities.

sections.heading: Necessity
sections.body: Tribunal of opinion that such facts cannot be found out unless restrictions are imposed.

sections.heading: Restrictions
sections.body: May cover transfer, exercise of voting or other rights, payment of dividends, or issue of further securities.

sections.heading: Duration
sections.body: Period not exceeding three years as specified in the order.

examples.title: Voting freeze during ownership probe
examples.body: During a s. 216 ownership investigation the Tribunal finds that voting rights on disputed shares must be frozen to ascertain true controllers. It may impose restrictions under s. 222 for a period not exceeding three years.

examples.title: Transfer restriction
examples.body: The Tribunal restricts transfer of specified securities so that the shareholding position is preserved while the investigation proceeds under s. 222.

hypotheticals.question: May restrictions under s. 222 last indefinitely?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 222 limits the period of restrictions to not exceeding three years as may be specified in the order.

distinctions.title: Restrictions upon securities (s. 222) vs freezing of assets (s. 221)
distinctions.left: Restrictions on transfer, voting, dividends or further issue of securities
distinctions.right: Freeze on transfer/removal/disposal of company funds, assets or properties

misconceptions.trap: Section 222 permanently cancels the securities subject to the order.
misconceptions.correction: Section 222 imposes time-limited restrictions on transfer, rights or further issue. It does not cancel the securities themselves.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 222 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Connect to s. 216 investigation or complaint. II. Test good reason and necessity. III. Apply restrictions within three-year limit. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Investigation link; facts about securities; restrictions sought; precise relief.

examTips: Linked to s. 216 ownership investigation or complaint.
Restrictions on transfer, voting, dividends, further issue.

learningObjectives: State when the Tribunal may restrict securities under s. 222.
Explain the types of restrictions and the three-year limit.
enhancement.definition: Section 222 empowers the Tribunal to impose time-limited restrictions on transfer, voting rights, dividends or further issue of securities where necessary to ascertain relevant facts in connection with an ownership investigation or complaint.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Securities rights may be temporarily restricted so that the true position can be ascertained during investigation without the position being changed by transfers or voting.
essentialIngredients: Connection with s. 216 investigation or complaint
Good reason to find relevant facts about securities
Restrictions necessary to find those facts
Order for period not exceeding three years
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 222 is the securities-restriction companion to ownership investigation under s. 216.
enhancement.problemApplication: Link to investigation; justify necessity; seek time-limited restrictions.
